newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan retail sales improving, but tempo still slow.
newsitem.headline: Japan retail sales improving, but tempo still slow.

text.p: Consumers spent a little more in Japan's department stores and retail chains this September compared with last year.

But there was no sign of any rapid recovery in the sales figures, which are widely used as the key pointers to economic growth trends, reflecting the slow pace of economic recovery and only moderate pay increases.

Sales at department stores rose 2.3 percent from a year earlier to 625.76 billion yen ($5.53 billion), the second consecutive month of year-on-year rises, the Japan Department Stores' Association announced on Thursday.
Overall sales were up in September, due to robust sales to individual shoppers but those to corporate customers remained weak.
Demand for seasonal items was active, it said.
Sales at chain stores rose a modest 0.9 percent year-on-year to 1.27 trillion yen ($11.2 billion) in September, but fell 8.9 percent from August, a chain store industry group announced separately.

Consumer appetite for autumn clothes was relatively active, but sales of fresh foods lacked steam as consumers were still concerned about a killer epidemic of food poisoning which swept Japan in the summer, the Japan Chain Stores' Association said in a statement.
Sales of outdoor goods and other items for leisure activities were slow due to the epidemic and unusually cool weather in early September, it said. ($=113 yen)
